info.name: ShipX Logistics API — Local
info.description:
Local development Postman collection for ShipX Logistics Platform.

## Setup
1. Start local services + bootstrap + migrate + seed: `make stack`
2. Start API server: `make dev`
3. Import this collection into Postman

## Auth
Auth is simulated via request headers (no JWT needed locally):
- `X-Tenant-ID`: tenant UUID
- `X-Role`: role name
- `X-User-ID`: user UUID

## Available Roles
- `nigeria_office_staff` — back-office staff (default)
- `tenant_admin` — tenant administrator
- `warehouse_attendant` — warehouse staff
- `customer` — customer
- `china_office_staff` — China-side staff
- `platform_admin` — platform superadmin

## Workflow
1. Create a Customer
2. Create a Container
3. Create a Packing List for the customer + container
4. Submit → Approve packing list (manifest auto-created)
5. Verify manifest
6. Generate billing → Confirm payment
7. Generate release note → Record pickup

request.description: Entra-only ROPC login proxy (Entra's token endpoint is CORS-blocked for the password grant). Returns {id_token, access_token, refresh_token}. 404 on Cognito. Username may be the real email; the backend maps it to the managed-domain UPN. Rate limited: 10 attempts/min per client address, and 5 failed passwords per 15 minutes per username; past either it returns 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with a Retry-After header.

Public customer self-registration against the company with slug {{tenant_slug}}. Answers 202 with {"data": {"status": "received"}} and no Location header WHETHER OR NOT the email already has an account, so it cannot be used to find out who is a customer (audit SEC-04). A new email gets the Cognito temporary-password email; an email that already has an account creates nothing and its owner is emailed instead. Rate limited to 5 per hour per client address (429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with Retry-After). notification_consent lists the channels offered for optional messages; an empty list is a recorded choice of none.

item.name: 1. Platform Admin
item.description:
Super-admin routes for managing tenants and platform settings.
Set X-Role to `platform_admin` for these endpoints.

query.description: Filter by action e.g. TENANT_UPDATED, TENANT_CREATED (optional)

request.description: GET /v1/platform/tenants/{id}/usage — per-tenant API usage breakdown (platform_admin)

item.name: 2. Tenant Admin
item.description:
Tenant configuration, users, charge types, and dollar rate.
Set X-Role to `tenant_admin` for these endpoints.

request.description:
Update a tenant user's full_name and/or role.

Supported fields:
- `full_name` (string): display name — synced to Cognito `name` attribute
- `role` (string): new role — synced to Cognito `custom:role` attribute

Email cannot be changed (Cognito login username is immutable).
PUT /v1/tenant/charge-types/{id} — update a charge type (tenant_admin)
DELETE /v1/tenant/charge-types/{id} — deactivate a charge type; returns 204 (tenant_admin)
DELETE /v1/tenant/users/{id} — deactivate a tenant user; returns 204 (tenant_admin)

item.name: 3. Customers
item.description: Customer management. Staff can create/update; customers can only read.

request.description:
Anonymise a customer record (GDPR Art. 17 — Right to Erasure).

Nulls all PII fields (name, email, phone, whatsapp, address, contract_details) and sets `anonymised_at`. The UUID shell is kept for FK integrity.

Requires: `tenant_admin` role.

Export all personal data held for a customer (GDPR Art. 20 — Right to Portability).

Returns a machine-readable JSON object containing:
- `customer`: profile data
- `billing_summary`: invoice history
- `shipments`: shipment tracking records
- `claims`: damage/missing/seized item claims
- `exported_at`: ISO timestamp

Requires: `tenant_admin` role.

Public endpoint — no auth required. Customer looks up shipment by tracking code + phone number.

The phone is normalised to E.164 before matching (fixed 2026-11-02). Customer phones are stored E.164 and this previously compared ONE exact string, so a local-format number never matched. Note this very request used phone=08012345678 — it would have returned 404 against a customer stored as +2348012345678. Both the normalised and the raw form are now accepted.

item.name: 5. Packing Lists
item.description: Packing list lifecycle: draft → submitted → approved/rejected → manifest auto-created on approval.

request.description:
Goods dates (both optional, both origin-side, validated in order):
- delivery_date - date the supplier DELIVERED the goods to the China warehouse. Cannot be in the future. This is NOT the expected customer delivery; that estimate lives on container.estimated_delivery_date.
- loading_date - date the goods were LOADED into the container. Must be on or after delivery_date (same day is allowed). Deliberately unbounded above: a packing list is written against a container still in 'loading' status, so a planned load date is legitimate.
Violations return 422. The rule is enforced on both POST and PUT.

item.name: Create Packing List — bulk quantity (identical packages)

request.description:
One line standing for 100 identical cartons. The server EXPANDS this into 100 item rows, each with its own carton_tag and its own CBM, sharing one batch_ref — it is not stored as quantity=100 on a single row, because nothing downstream multiplies CBM by quantity and the line would otherwise bill as one carton.

identical_confirmed MUST be true whenever quantity > 1; omitting it returns 422. quantity is capped at 500.

Expect 100 entries in the response's items[], tags running ...-001 to ...-100.

item.name: 6. Manifests
item.description: Manifests are auto-created when a packing list is approved. Use verify to confirm cargo against physical arrival.

item.name: 7. Billing
item.description: Billing records, charges, storage fees, disputes, and carryovers.

query.description: Free-text search: invoice number, customer name, or container number

request.description: Generate invoices for a cleared container. With customer_id: invoices that customer (201), or 422 with a rule (CONTAINER_NOT_CLEARED, CUSTOMER_NOT_ON_CONTAINER, ALREADY_BILLED, NO_CBM, RATE_CONFIG_MISSING). Omit customer_id to invoice every customer on the container who has none yet (200, per-customer results). Idempotent per customer + container.

One billing record by its OWN id. Distinct from "Get Billing for Customer" above, which takes a *customer* id at the bare /v1/billing/{id} shape — both ids are UUIDs, so the by-id read needs the /detail suffix. Response is byte-identical to the matching row from List Billing Records. Customer role is scoped to its own records (403 otherwise).

One dispute with its measurement data: customer, container, billed CBM, the customer's measured CBM and reason, and the approved packing-list lines the CBM was summed from. No amount, rate or payment, so china_office_staff (who may resolve disputes but not read invoices) can use it as well as nigeria_office_staff and tenant_admin. 404 for an unknown id.
PATCH /v1/billing/carryovers/{id}/exempt — mark a carryover as exempted (tenant_admin)
POST /v1/billing/disputes — staff-created CBM dispute (billing_id in body; tenant_admin or nigeria_office_staff)
PATCH /v1/billing/disputes/{id}/reject — reject a CBM dispute with a reason (tenant_admin or nigeria_office_staff)
Customers on a cleared container who have CBM to bill and no live invoice (tenant_admin, nigeria_office_staff). Feeds the dashboard queue; complete with POST /v1/billing { container_id }.

item.name: 8. Claims
item.description: Damage claims, missing items, and seized items. Use presigned URL to upload evidence photos.

request.description: One claim. Staff read any claim; a customer reads only their own and gets 404 for anyone else's (not 403, which would confirm the id exists). Response adds `evidence` (each file with a 5-minute `download_url`), `resolution` (decision, amount and `reason`; never the approver or approval level) and `refund` ({id, status, amount_ngn}) alongside the claim fields. `resolution.reason` is what staff typed when deciding: staff always get it; a customer gets it only when the decision went against them (`no_action`), and null for a refund, compensation or discount.

body.raw:
{
  "resolution_type": "refund",
  "amount_usd": 80.00,
  "amount_ngn": 132000.00,
  "reason": "Water damage confirmed during inspection. Partial refund for value of damaged goods.",
  "notes": "Customer accepted refund offer"
}

request.description: Decide a claim. `reason` is required (422) when `resolution_type` is `no_action`: the customer is shown it on their claim page, word for word. For `refund`, `compensation` and `discount` the reason is staff's internal record and is never returned to the customer.
nigeria_office_staff, tenant_admin and (2026-11-16) china_office_staff, who record the supply and loading check.

A refund amount or any other status from China is 403; changing an item already confirmed_lost or resolved is 422 MISSING_ITEM_ALREADY_DECIDED.

Confirms the item lost. With refund_amount_ngn (> 0) it opens one refund_request (refund_type missing_item, pending_review) linked to the item; leave it out to confirm the loss without compensation. status must be reported, investigating, found_and_shipping, confirmed_lost or resolved; a bad status or amount is 422.

request.description:
Add a branch/office warehouse. tenant_admin only.

`is_default` (optional, default false) promotes it to the tenant's default as part of creating it. The FIRST warehouse a tenant creates becomes the default regardless - nothing else sets is_default, and a tenant without one cannot generate a release note.

409 DUPLICATE_RESOURCE if an ACTIVE warehouse already has this name. A retired (is_active=false) warehouse does NOT reserve its name - uniqueness is scoped to active rows (migration 056).

`country` (migration 057, default 'Nigeria') is the branch's destination country. It anchors the state/province picker in the UI; without it `state` could only be free text.

PERMANENTLY delete a warehouse. tenant_admin only.

A real delete, not a flag flip: the row is removed and its name becomes reusable.

Refusals (422 BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION, with `rule_id`):
- WAREHOUSE_IN_USE - a release_note / pickup_record / payment_record / packing_list references it. Those records must keep the warehouse they were issued against, so use 'Deactivate Warehouse (retire)' instead.
- WAREHOUSE_DEFAULT_IMMUTABLE - set another warehouse as default first.
- WAREHOUSE_LAST_ACTIVE - a tenant must keep at least one active warehouse.

Retire a warehouse without deleting it (is_active = false). tenant_admin only.

The path for a warehouse that handover documents reference, so DELETE refuses it. It stops appearing in pickers, those records keep their history, and its name becomes reusable (uniqueness is scoped to active rows).

Same default-warehouse and last-active guards as DELETE.

tenant_admin, nigeria_office_staff. Sends the customer a fresh six digit pickup code for an active release note by SMS and email, retires the old one and unlocks the note. Response: `{release_note_id, sent_via}`; the code is never returned. Needs PICKUP_CODE_PEPPER. To record a pickup for a note with a code, add `"pickup_code": "123456"` to the PATCH .../release body.

item.name: 10. Refunds
item.description:
Refund request workflow: create → accounts review → approve/reject.
Types: overpayment | cbm_correction | damage_or_loss

request.description: One refund request. A customer reads only their own, and gets a customer view: `reason` only when they raised the request themselves (a refund raised from a claim decision carries staff's internal reason, which is not theirs to read), `rejection_reason` always, and null for `approval_level`, `debt_check_passed`, `debt_check_notes` and `threshold`.

Every container matching the container list's filters and sort. china_office_staff, nigeria_office_staff and tenant_admin. Same format and size rules as the invoice-list export.
